title: Item Image Prompt Context Refinement

title: Analytics Expansion — 20 New Metrics

Adds unanimous vote tracking to existing voting stats. 25 new tests.

title: Location Image Prompt Context Refinement
description: Refine location entity context for image generation prompts — prioritize name, description, and lore as primary visual signals. Include tags, location_type, coordinates as secondary context. Expand features with full descriptions and types for richer LLM input. Mirrors F-049 item prompt approach

title: Chat Absent Response Handling
description: Gracefully handle API failures for individual participants in chat. When a council member or character fails to respond, inject [absent] Was unavailable to respond at this time. [/absent] and continue to the next participant instead of crashing the stream. Covers all 4 chat methods: get_agent_response, get_agent_response_streaming, continue_conversation, continue_conversation_streaming. Frontend renders [absent] tags with distinct amber styling.

title: LLM Injection System
description: User-authored llm_injection text fields on items, locations, and stores that are injected into LLM context alongside existing layers (laws, memories, characters). Non-consumable items have static injections; consumable items have 24h TTL injections. Stores now appear in participant context with their injection text. Frontend create/edit forms updated with injection textareas and active/expired badges.

title: Injection Text Length Limits
description: Configurable per-entity character limits for llm_injection fields: items 500, locations 800, stores 500. Enforced at backend validation (create/update reject with helpful error), context builder truncation (replaced hardcoded :300 with configurable limits), and frontend (maxlength + live character counters with amber/red threshold feedback). API responses include injection_max_length metadata. 26 new tests.

title: Eliminate Explore Chat Context Duplication
description: When explore/story chat triggers agent responses, MemoryInfluence injects world locations+items AND _build_participant_context also injects them — same data, twice. Add skip_world_context parameter to _build_participant_context so chat callers skip world entities (MemoryInfluence already handles them with relevance scoring). Saves ~500–1500 tokens per chat turn in explore mode.

title: Skip Self-Persona Preview in Participant Context
description: Remove redundant persona preview from _build_participant_context when the member IS the current speaker — they already have their full system_prompt as the system message. Add current_speaker parameter to skip that member's 500-char persona preview. Saves ~125 tokens per turn per active member.

title: Global Token Budget / Context Window Manager
description: ContextBudget class that accepts a target token count (e.g. 32,768) and allocates portions to each layer with priorities: system prompt (fixed, highest), conversation history (sliding window, high), memories/beliefs (scored, medium), world context (scored, lower), LLM injections (user-controlled, lowest). Each layer truncates to fit the budget, making context size predictable regardless of world size.

title: Rolling Conversation Summary
description: For conversations with >10 messages, generate a cached rolling LLM summary of messages 1–N, then inject [Summary of prior conversation: ...] + last 5 messages instead of raw last 10. Preserves context continuity while cutting ~500–2000 tokens in long conversations.

title: Lazy/Cached Memory Scoring
description: Cache MemoryContext results for a given (member, topic_hash) pair. Only re-score when the topic meaningfully changes (keyword diff). Add stale_after TTL (e.g. 5 minutes). Negligible token savings but significant latency improvement.

title: Conditional Law Injection
description: Score laws against context keywords (same as memories) and only inject relevant ones. A law about taxation rates should not appear when discussing character backstories. Saves ~50–200 tokens when most laws are irrelevant.

title: Tiered Injection Profiles
description: Define injection profiles: chat_full (system prompt + history + memory + world + injections), chat_light (system prompt + history + identity), image_gen (entity context + style only), narration (story context + participant identity + relevant world subset), discussion (proposal + prior contributions + member beliefs only). Let each route choose the appropriate profile. Saves ~1000–2000 tokens for lightweight call types.

title: Aggressive Character Preview Truncation
description: Reduce character backstory preview from 500 to 200 chars in _build_participant_context. The backstory preview is for OTHER participants to know who is in the room, not for the character to know their own backstory (which is already in their system prompt). Saves ~200–500 tokens with multiple characters.

title: Split human_chat.py Into Focused Modules
description: human_chat.py is 1,557 lines / 57KB — the largest module. Split into focused sub-modules: (1) Extract streaming logic (get_agent_response_streaming, continue_conversation_streaming) into core/chat_streaming.py, (2) Move character-to-member conversion helpers (_character_to_member, _character_memory_name) into core/characters.py as public utility functions, (3) Move _build_human_chat_prompt() into core/prompt_builder.py or a new core/chat_prompt.py. Goal: reduce human_chat.py to ~800 lines focused on lifecycle management (create, send, close, add/remove participants). All tests must continue passing with import path updates.

title: Extract Business Logic From Route Files
description: Several route files contain substantial business logic that should live in core/ modules. Primary target: _build_participant_context() in routes/explore.py (350-line prompt assembly engine) should move to core/context_builder.py or core/prompt_builder.py. Secondary: examine routes/stories.py (46KB) and routes/proposals.py (39KB) for business logic that could be extracted. Routes should ideally be thin HTTP adapters — parse request, call business logic, return response. Update all imports and tests. No behavior changes.

title: Add Exception Logging to Silent Catch Blocks
description: Multiple modules use bare 'except Exception: pass' that silently swallow errors, making debugging difficult. Key locations: (1) _build_participant_context() in routes/explore.py — memory influence, registry, character, law, location, item, and store loading all have silent catches, (2) human_chat.py streaming methods, (3) routes/stories.py scene/chat handlers, (4) routes/sessions.py analytics. Replace bare 'except Exception: pass' with 'except Exception: logger.debug("...", exc_info=True)' or logger.warning for more critical paths. Ensure each module has a module-level logger via logging.getLogger(__name__). No behavior changes — just visibility into failures.

title: Thread-Safe Sequential ID Generation
description: All _next_id() implementations (CharacterManager, ProposalManager, CustomStylePresetManager, StoryManager, ExplorationManager, etc.) scan the filesystem for existing files and increment — susceptible to race conditions under concurrent API requests. Two concurrent calls could get the same ID; the second atomic_write would silently overwrite the first. Fix: add a per-manager threading.Lock around ID generation + file creation as an atomic unit. Alternatively, consider a shared atomic counter file or UUID-based IDs. Primary targets: CharacterManager._next_id(), ProposalManager._next_id(), CustomStylePresetManager._next_id(), StoryManager._next_id(), ExplorationManager._next_scene_id(). Add concurrent-creation tests to verify safety.

title: Item Owned-By Multi-Owner Field
description: Replace the single-string 'owner' field on Items with a multi-owner 'owned_by' list. Each entry has a name and type (user, character, council_member). Supports multiple simultaneous owners. Backward compatible — legacy 'owner' strings auto-migrate to owned_by on load. Dedicated PUT /api/items/{id}/owned-by endpoint. Frontend add/remove owner UI with type badges. Validation: non-empty name, valid type, no duplicate name+type pairs.

title: Gift Giving System
description: Gift-giving mechanism that transfers item ownership via owned_by changes. When a gift is given, the item's owned_by list is updated to reflect the new owner, and a simple chat message exchange is auto-created between the gift receiver and gift giver acknowledging the gift. Depends on the owned_by multi-owner field (F-067) and chat system (F-009).

title: Reputation System
description: Event-sourced reputation tracking for council members and characters. Immutable events are stored as JSONL, scores computed on demand with 120-day half-life decay. Six tiers from Disgraced to Legendary. Default reputation stance per entity (configurable first impression). API endpoints for leaderboard, scoring, event history, and manual admin awards. Frontend leaderboard and detail views. LLM context injection of reputation tiers. Infrastructure-only — automated event recording from votes/proposals/gifts is deferred to F-070.

title: Reputation Auto-Recording Integration
description: Wire automated reputation event recording into existing systems. When a vote is cast, proposal authored/approved/rejected, gift given/received, discussion participated in, or council session attended, a reputation event is automatically recorded. Requires careful integration hooks in VotingEngine, ProposalManager, ItemManager.gift_item, DiscussionManager, and SessionManager. Should be minimally invasive — thin observer/hook layer.

title: Reputation Gameplay Effects
description: Reputation scores affect gameplay mechanics. IMPORTANT: Do not implement without a full discussion and approved implementation plan. Potential effects: vote weight modulation based on reputation tier, store price adjustments, proposal fast-track for high-reputation authors, restricted actions for disgraced entities. Requires careful balancing to avoid feedback loops.

title: Gifting Section Web UI
description: Dedicated top-level Gifting view in the web dashboard. Centralises all gift-giving into one page with item selector, owner/recipient pickers (autocomplete from council members and characters), gift message field, reputation gain preview (+5 giver / +1 receiver), and a reverse-chronological gift history timeline. New GET /api/gifts/history endpoint reads H-GIFT-*.json chat records for the history view.

title: Gift Task Integration
description: Connects the Task system to the Gifting system. Users can create tasks with task_type='gift' and a gift_config specifying item, giver, recipient, and message. When DoTasks completes a gift task, it automatically executes the gift transfer (ItemManager.gift_item), creates a chat record (_create_gift_chat), and fires reputation hooks (on_gift_given). The SSE feed emits a gift_complete event with a celebration card (animated gradient border, confetti, pulsing gift icon). Task detail shows a Gift Delivered banner for completed gift tasks and a Gift Configuration info section. Task table rows display a gift badge for gift-type tasks.

title: Character Memory Auto-Creation
description: When a new character is created, automatically create a per-character memory directory (using character_memory_name convention) so the character appears in the Memories section. Character memories are shown alongside council member memories in the Memories view with distinct character badges. Memory detail view supports browsing character beliefs and events.

title: Memory Decay, Summarization & Contested Memories
description: Integrate the memory decay/summarization/contested-memory subsystems into the running application. EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE: core/memory_influence.py already has _compute_decay_factor() (exponential half-life formula with configurable 30-day half-life, 0.1 floor), score_memories() applies decay to relevance scores and annotates reasons with freshness %. config/settings.py already defines MEMORY_DECAY_ENABLED/HALF_LIFE/MIN_FACTOR, MEMORY_SUMMARIZATION_ENABLED/KEEP_RECENT/SESSION_THRESHOLD, and CONTESTED_MEMORY_ENABLED/PROBABILITY. core/memory.py has get_unique_session_ids(), get_sessions_needing_summary(), write_summarized_entry(), read_summarized_log(), record_contested_memory(), read_contested_memories(), get_contested_for_event(). tests/test_memory_decay.py has 731 lines / ~45 tests covering all three subsystems. NEEDED: (1) Settings UI — expose decay half-life, min factor, summarization threshold, contested probability, and enable/disable toggles in the web Settings page so users can tune without editing settings.py. (2) API endpoints — GET/PUT /api/settings/memory-decay for current config + update, POST /api/memories/{member}/summarize to trigger LLM summarization on demand, GET /api/memories/{member}/contested for viewing contested memories. (3) Memory detail UI — show contested memory sub-bullets in the Memories detail view, show summarized entries with distinct styling, show decay freshness indicators on memory cards. (4) Automatic summarization trigger — optionally run summarize_sessions_llm as a background task when session count exceeds threshold. (5) Contested memory generation — wire maybe_generate_contested_memory into chat response paths (human_chat.py get_agent_response) so a small % of memories get contested variants.

title: Narrative Engine Dashboard Integration
description: Wire the existing NarrativeEngine into the web dashboard as a live news ticker / bulletin feed. EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE: core/narrative_engine.py (502 lines) is fully implemented with NarrativeBulletin dataclass, 7 template banks (proposals created/decided, votes approved/rejected/vetoed, characters created/activated, items, locations, treasury), randomized selection, time-window filtering, and max-bulletin capping. GET /api/narrative-bulletins endpoint already exists in core/routes/status.py and is tested (tests/test_narrative_engine.py, 628 lines, ~35 tests). config/settings.py has NARRATIVE_MAX_BULLETINS=10 and NARRATIVE_MAX_AGE_DAYS=30. NEEDED: (1) Dashboard UI component — a scrolling/animated news ticker or bulletin feed panel on the main Dashboard view (js/dashboard.js) that fetches /api/narrative-bulletins and renders headline cards with emoji icons, source type badges, timestamps, and clickable links to the source entity detail page. (2) CSS module — css/narrative.css with ticker animation, bulletin card styling, source-type color coding, and responsive layout. (3) Auto-refresh — polling or visibility-based refresh (every 60s or on page focus). (4) Settings integration — expose NARRATIVE_MAX_BULLETINS and NARRATIVE_MAX_AGE_DAYS in the Settings UI. (5) Optional: bulletin history/archive view accessible from the dashboard.

title: Embedding-Based Semantic Memory Retrieval
description: Upgrade memory scoring from optional/fallback embeddings to a first-class semantic retrieval system with user-visible controls. EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE: core/embeddings.py (176 lines) provides EmbeddingProvider with lazy-loading sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 default), singleton pattern, similarity(), batch_similarity(), encode(), and graceful fallback when not installed. core/memory_influence.py already does hybrid scoring (EMBEDDING_SIMILARITY_WEIGHT * cosine + EMBEDDING_JACCARD_WEIGHT * jaccard) with automatic fallback to pure Jaccard when unavailable. config/settings.py has EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME, EMBEDDING_SIMILARITY_WEIGHT, EMBEDDING_JACCARD_WEIGHT. tests/test_embeddings.py (221 lines, ~21 tests) covers init, availability, similarity, batch, encode, singleton, and cosine math. NEEDED: (1) Settings UI — display embedding model status (loaded/unavailable), model name, allow toggling between semantic+keyword hybrid vs keyword-only mode, adjust weights. (2) Installation helper — Settings page guidance or one-click install prompt for sentence-transformers+torch when not available. (3) Memory Explorer integration — show scoring mode indicator (semantic vs keyword) in Memory detail views, display similarity scores alongside keyword match reasons. (4) Performance monitoring — track and display embedding encode latency in analytics or settings, cache embeddings for frequently-accessed beliefs. (5) Model selection — allow choosing between embedding models (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, all-mpnet-base-v2, etc.) from settings with lazy reload.

title: Dashboard Activity Feed & Summary Enhancements
description: Enhance the main web Dashboard beyond its current static status-card layout into a dynamic activity hub. EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE: core/dashboard.py (727 lines) provides the Rich terminal DashboardRenderer for CLI with status panels, analytics overview, member stats, evolution timelines, and version diffs. The web dashboard (js/dashboard.js) currently shows static count cards for members, proposals, votes, characters, etc. fetched from GET /api/status. The narrative engine (F-076) will add a bulletin feed, but the dashboard itself needs richer composition. NEEDED: (1) Activity timeline — a reverse-chronological feed of recent system events (new proposals, votes cast, characters created/evolved, gifts given, tasks completed) pulled from multiple data sources, displayed as a unified scrollable timeline with entity-type icons and clickable links. (2) Quick-action buttons — create proposal, start chat, run task, give gift directly from dashboard without navigating. (3) System health panel — embedding status, LLM provider connectivity, storage usage, memory cache hit rates. (4) At-a-glance world summary — styled cards showing world entity counts with sparkline trends or recent-change indicators instead of plain numbers. (5) Responsive layout — card grid that reflows elegantly on mobile/tablet. (6) Welcome state — an attractive empty-state when the system is fresh with guided onboarding steps.

title: Explore Section Refinement — Feature-Centric Movement
description: Transforms the Explore section from static look-around into a stateful, progressive exploration experience. IMPLEMENTED: (1) ExplorationState engine (core/exploration_state.py) — tracks current focus, explored areas, mode (guided/imaginative), and scene setting per location. (2) Smart prompt builder (ExplorationManager.build_focused_prompt) — three-phase prompting: initial exterior overview, guided feature-focused exploration, and imaginative discovery beyond the defined map. (3) Movement UI — frontend movement panel with clickable feature cards, progress bar, mode badge, and reset button. (4) Exploration state endpoints — GET /state, POST /state/reset, and target-aware POST /look-around. (5) Location dynamism inference — classifies locations as static/dynamic/moderate for imaginative mode directives. (6) Scene focus_area tracking — each generated scene records which area it depicts. (7) Indoor/outdoor inference from feature types and ComfyUI prompt keywords.
